first_comment: The straight-tusked elephant was one of the biggest land mammals of the Ice Age, and its tooth still held pollen clues from reeds, willows and wetlands. Would you have wanted to see one? 🐘

stories.headline: A giant elephant's tooth reveals a lost Ice Age oasis
stories.summary: Found next to stone handaxes at Gesher Benot Ya'aqov, a straight-tusked elephant's molar showed rivers, wetlands and woods that fed huge animals and early humans.
stories.why: Oases like this may have helped early humans travel between Africa and Eurasia.

stories.stat_label: years: age of the oldest ice
stories.headline: Ice in Tibet turned out to be over 128,000 years old
stories.summary: Cores drilled 23 years apart, in 1992 and 2015, matched closely. New dating puts the Guliya ice beyond 128,000 years, over 100,000 years older than the region's known record.
stories.why: Outside the poles, it is the only mountain ice known to keep climate records this old.

stories.headline: Pure cranberry juice slowed tooth plaque in a small trial
stories.summary: Children and adults who swished unsweetened 100% cranberry juice saw slower plaque regrowth and less acid, which harms enamel. Sugary juice drinks and water didn't do the same.
stories.why: A tart drink could one day become a natural mouth rinse, though bigger studies are needed.

stories.stat_label: the year this carbon metal was predicted
stories.headline: 30 years after it was predicted, a carbon 'metal' was built
stories.summary: Chemists at USTC built ultrathin ribbons of only 5- and 7-sided carbon rings on silver. Lifted with a microscope tip, one version carried current like a true metal.
stories.why: Carbon wires could replace metal ones that overheat as chips keep shrinking.

fun_fact: The Guliya ice cores were drilled 23 years apart, yet their climate signals matched.
